title: ArthriMove — Mom's Exercise App
summary: Exercise app for elderly with arthritis. The twist: sending mom a laptop and letting her build it herself with guided AI assistance.

overview.what: A gentle daily exercise app for elderly people with arthritis — chair-based routines, voice guidance, pain check-ins, caregiver dashboard. But the real project is the process: setting up mom with a laptop and AI tools so she can shape the app herself, giving her ownership of something meaningful.
overview.status_detail: Concept defined. Need to figure out the flow for mom — what laptop, what tools, how to guide her remotely.

columns.name: Set up mom's laptop
values: Buy a laptop, set up dev environment, ship it to her
Research best laptop for a non-technical user ($300-500 Chromebook or MacBook Air?)

columns.name: Design the guided flow
values: How does mom interact with the build process?
Options: Claude Code on her machine, a no-code builder like Cursor/Replit, or a guided template she customizes

columns.name: Define MVP features
values: Core: daily exercise video/animation, pain check-in (1-5), streak tracker, large text UI

columns.name: Exercise content
values: Research: partner with a PT? Use existing public domain chair yoga content? Mom designs based on her experience?

columns.name: Caregiver dashboard
values: Family can see mom's progress remotely
Simple: daily completion status, pain trend graph, streak — visible via shared link

considerations.label: Mom's tech level
considerations.detail: Need to assess: can she use a browser? Copy/paste? Follow step-by-step video instructions? This determines the whole approach.

considerations.label: The real value
considerations.detail: It's not just the app — it's mom learning to build something with technology. The process matters as much as the product.

considerations.label: Remote support
considerations.detail: You're in NYC, she's not. Need a way to help her remotely — screen sharing, video calls, or an AI assistant on her machine.

considerations.label: Market potential
considerations.detail: 58M arthritis sufferers in US. Most PT apps ignore 65+ UX. If the app works for mom, it could work for millions.

considerations.label: Platform choice
considerations.detail: Web app (works on any device, no app store) vs native (better for notifications, offline). Web-first is simpler for mom to test.

notes:
The interesting angle here: mom isn't just the user — she's the co-builder. She knows the pain points better than any developer. The question is finding the right level of abstraction so she can contribute meaningfully without needing to code.

Possible flows:
1. Send her a MacBook Air with Claude Code installed. Walk her through prompting it to build screens.
2. Set up a Replit/Glitch project she can edit in-browser. You handle the hard parts, she customizes content/flow.
3. Build a template app, give her a simple admin panel to add exercises, adjust text, set schedule.

Option 3 is probably most realistic. Option 1 is most ambitious and coolest story.
